extracted.intended_audience: Undergraduate and graduate-level mathematics students; general mathematical audience.
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for mathematics graduate students and early-career mathematicians on making key decisions and handling practical aspects of graduate school and the early academic career (choosing programs, exams, advisor, thesis, jobs, and understanding departmental structure).

rubrics_metrics.name: Choosing a program
rubrics_metrics.description: Addresses the major issues of graduate school, including choosing a program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The book offers detailed guidance to help students navigate graduate school decisions (implicitly evaluating programs on fit, resources, advisor availability, and future career prospects). Avoids generalities and aims to give clear, practical advice on how to handle real situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Passing the qualifying exams
rubrics_metrics.description: Addresses the major issues of graduate school, including passing the qualifying exams.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides concrete advice on preparing for and succeeding at qualifying exams (study strategies, expectations, and common pitfalls), presented in a forthright, practical style rather than abstract generalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finding an advisor
rubrics_metrics.description: Addresses the major issues of graduate school, including finding an advisor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance likely covers how to select, approach, and work with an advisor, what to expect from the advisor–student relationship, and how that choice affects career trajectory; emphasis on practical, situation-based advice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing a thesis
rubrics_metrics.description: Addresses the major issues of graduate school, including writing a thesis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses the process and expectations for thesis research and writing, including organization, scope, and completion strategies; presented with clear, actionable recommendations rather than vague statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Getting the first job
rubrics_metrics.description: Addresses the major issues of graduate school, including getting that first job.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offers advice on the academic job market and early-career job-seeking (applications, interviews, negotiation, and expectations for entry-level positions), with practical tips drawn from the author's experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description of the basic elements of a mathematical education
rubrics_metrics.description: The book contains a description of the basic elements of a mathematical education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Surveys foundational components that students should acquire during their education (likely coursework, problem-solving techniques, breadth vs. depth), framing these as benchmarks for progress through graduate training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Glossary and appendices on departmental/university structure
rubrics_metrics.description: The book contains a glossary and appendices on the structure of a typical department and university.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides reference material explaining institutional organization and administrative structures so students can understand roles, processes, and where to seek resources or decisions within academia.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanation of standard academic ranks
rubrics_metrics.description: The book contains appendices on the standard academic ranks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies the hierarchy and expectations associated with academic titles (e.g., instructor, assistant professor, associate professor, full professor), helping readers set realistic career goals and understand promotion processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical, forthright style (avoid generalities)
rubrics_metrics.description: The author 'avoids generalities, giving clear advice on how to handle real situations.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes concrete, situation-based advice and real-world examples as preferred over abstract, general recommendations; implies that useful guidance should be specific, actionable, and experience-based.
